correctness.rationale: For the exact two-patch growth--dispersal recursion, population-total column sums give a strategy-normalized mean-one martingale. At q=1/(1+s) the dispersal matrix has identical rows, and normalized abundance is a product of independent annual average growth factors. Under spatially exchangeable shocks, symmetrization and Jensen give a conditional convex test inequality. Its averaging operator preserves convexity, yielding the all-horizon order by induction. The strict equality classification follows from positivity and the impossibility of a deterministic nonunit growth ratio under a nondegenerate exchangeable law. Conditioning the next squared multiplier proves the displayed two-year gap exactly; square-integrability supplies the variance floor. The direct full-path exact Fraction checker passed 6022 assertions but cannot replace the analytic proof. The argument is limited to temporally independent years, exchangeable positive growth and strategy-specific mean normalization.

originality.rationale: The 2012 primary article states the exact growth--dispersal matrix, full-mixing condition, stationary ratio dynamics and logarithmic growth; the 2013 extension studies global coupling and large-population growth variance. The 1998 sink-habitat article and 2010 spatial-growth analysis focus on geometric population persistence. General convex order and static Jensen symmetrization are acknowledged known tools. The proposed precise contribution is a distribution-free finite-horizon convex-order ranking for mean-normalized total abundance, strict unique survivor-adjusted optimum and exact two-year gap. These conclusions are not present in the inspected technical texts. Search coverage cannot establish global priority; uninspected papers and potential implicit applications of dynamic diversification theory remain a serious historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority remains provisional: older dynamic-diversification literature or full text of Keeling (2000) and Schreiber (2010) might contain an equivalent general theorem.
The convex symmetrization device is a standard inequality, so the novelty claim is confined to exact dynamic metapopulation implications and strict classification, not the abstract inequality.
Only mean-normalized abundance is ordered: actual mortality-adjusted total population may prefer a different migration fraction.
No independent scientific validation has yet been performed.

value.rationale: The cited ecological model examines environmental risk spreading but exact across-time total-abundance distributional comparisons are not addressed in its principal growth-rate results. The theorem supplies the complete sharp optimum simultaneously for every finite time and every convex measure of relative population risk, including shortfall and exceedance losses, under arbitrary within-year habitat correlation. Its exact two-year formula quantifies the penalty from imperfect mixing, detects the first year where the policy matters, and makes migrant mortality enter the optimum as q=1/(1+s). Unlike a mere low-order moment computation, the universal convex order allows comparison of entire normalized outcome distributions. The physical limitation that absolute population survival and growth are not optimized is explicitly disclosed.
